title: Compact component contrast mapper for brand integrations
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary: Create a compact, deterministic token-mapping approach to adapt brand colors into the console's dense component surfaces (small buttons, compact table rows, sparklines and micro charts) when running in dark and high-contrast modes. Goal is to preserve brand recognition while meeting accessibility contrast targets for interaction affordances and data ink in small UI elements.

Context: During the theming review for Console vNext we observed several brand integrations (customer-provided accent palettes) that produce legibility and visibility regressions in compact components in dark mode: low-contrast button labels, invisible table row separators, and chart sparkline strokes that disappear on certain brand variants. The platform must support customer brand accents without requiring bespoke CSS per customer.

Design proposition: Implement a token-mapping layer specific to compact surfaces that: (1) derives a semantic intent from incoming brand accent tokens (accent-primary, accent-weak, accent-strong), (2) computes contrast-safe derivatives for small text and thin strokes using perceptual adjustments instead of naive alpha overlays, and (3) exposes a small set of maintainable override tokens for components to consume: compact-ink, compact-stroke, compact-hover, compact-focus-outline.

Key heuristics and algorithm notes: - Use relative luminance + CIEDE2000 thresholds to decide whether to desaturate, brighten, or add a subtle luminance overlay for brand-derived accents on dark surfaces. - For micro strokes (<=1.5px visual weight) aim for at least 3:1 contrast relative to surface for recognition (but maintain 4.5:1 for text where applicable). - Prefer luminance-preserving desaturation over pure opacity overlays when the accent hue causes hue-shift artifacts on charts. - Quantize resulting values into a small palette (6 variants) to avoid token explosion across themes and to make QA snapshots deterministic.

Trade-offs considered: - Preserving exact brand hue vs meeting contrast: we bias toward contrast for interactive affordances (buttons, focus rings), but allow closer hue fidelity for non-interactive decorative accents (avatars, large brand badges). - Algorithmic mapping complexity vs. maintainability: chose a small set of tunable heuristics (lum delta + chroma clamp) rather than heavy ML-based color transforms to keep behaviour predictable and reviewable. - Token proliferation vs. per-component overrides: we create semantic compact tokens consumed by components rather than adding component-specific brand tokens.

Design deliverables: - Token spec (compact-ink, compact-stroke, compact-hover, compact-focus-outline) with color examples across 8 sample brand palettes. - Component override guidance for Button (compact), Table (dense rows), Chart (sparkline stroke and point highlight), Table-row hover/selected states. - Visual QA checklist and Percy story list for regression snapshots.

Links and artifacts: - Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONS/Compact+Component+Contrast+Mapper - Working Figma board: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/compact-theming-experiments - Design tokens spreadsheet (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/compact-token-experiments - GitHub PR prototype (token mapping lib): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2743 - Percy visual test grouping: https://percy.io/redwood/console/compact-theming

Open questions: - Should compact-focus-outline be larger for keyboard users on compact controls? Accessibility team suggests keeping visual focus at least 3px for small targets (see comment below). - Do we allow customers to opt-out of compact token remapping? Security/enterprise team asked about an allowlist for fully-preserved brand modes (follow-up ENG ticket requested).
acceptance_criteria: Define and publish compact token spec in token registry and Confluence
Add token mapping routine in token-service with unit tests and example mapping for 8 sample brand palettes
Update compact Button, Table (dense), and Chart stories to consume new tokens
Percy snapshot baseline created and no visual regressions on 6 major brand examples
Accessibility audit confirms compact text meets 4.5:1 where applicable and micro strokes meet 3:1 threshold
